job: Shipping reproducible sub-2-bit selective-precision GGUF recipes that fit a 700B-plus open-weight model into 256GB or less of single-node memory
outcome: A published, reproducible quantization recipe running a frontier-class open-weight model on one workstation node under 256GB combined memory
motivation: Owning the canonical local-inference recipe for the heaviest open tier drives adoption and cements the toolkit as the on-prem standard

task.who: the toolkit's quantization and kernel engineering team
task.what: Refine selective sub-2-bit quant recipe and publish it
task.where: Dynamic GGUF build pipeline and public model-hub release
task.why: A reproducible recipe is what crosses the heaviest tier on-prem
task.how: Selective-precision sub-2-bit GGUF quantization with documented steps

job: Independently rerunning the published recipe on owned hardware and measuring accuracy retention on a public benchmark rather than vendor self-report
outcome: A third-party reproduction confirming the sub-256GB single-node run with public-benchmark accuracy retention published openly
motivation: Vendor compression and quality numbers are self-reported and unverified, so credible independent confirmation is what the community trusts

task.who: an independent researcher or local-LLM community benchmarker
task.what: Reproduce the run and publish accuracy-retention scores
task.where: Owned single-node workstation and a public benchmark harness
task.why: Self-reported quality numbers need independent verification to be trusted
task.how: Public coding and reasoning benchmark on the quantized build

job: Releasing a near-frontier 700B-plus mixture-of-experts open-weight checkpoint and weights that the quantization recipe can compress and run single-node
outcome: An available open-weight frontier-class checkpoint whose released weights enable a sub-256GB single-node quantized deployment
motivation: Open releases that demonstrably run on owned hardware drive ecosystem reach and differentiate the lab against closed cloud-only frontier rivals

task.who: the lab's open-weight release and model-publishing function
task.what: Publish full-precision frontier-class MoE weights openly
task.where: Public model hub and the lab's release channels
task.when: Ahead of and through 2026 into Q4
task.why: Open weights are the raw input the quantization recipe needs
task.how: Open-weight checkpoint release in a standard inference format
